newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HUNGARY INTEREST RATE DECLINE SLOWS IN Q2 - C.BANK.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARY INTEREST RATE DECLINE SLOWS IN Q2 - C.BANK.

text.p: A two-year-long trend of interest rate decline in Hungary's corporate banking has slowed down in the second quarter of the year, the National Bank of Hungary (NBH) said in a statement on Friday.
"The trend of interest rate decline beginning in the autumn of 1995, has slowed down in the past few months," it said.

The average interest rate on shorter than one year corporate loans was down at 22 percent in June from 27.4 percent one year before, but fell only 0.4 percentage points from March and were unchanged compared with May, it said.
The average interest rate on shorter than one year deposits dropped to 17.6 percent in June from 20.5 one year before, 18.2 percent in March and 17.9 percent in May.
The short-term average interest rate margin widened in June to 4.4 percent from May's record low level of 4.1 percent.
The demand for corporate loans extended in forint increased substantially in June, the NBH added.

It said that the stock of shorter-than-one-year loan contracts concluded in June rose by more than 30 percent to 33.7 billion forints from May, and for loans with longer maturities by almost 25 percent to 15.8 billion forints.
